objective: Verify the private client document lifecycle from upload through scoped download, review and recovery.
scope: Bounded uploads, type validation and explicit antivirus verdict
Lead-scoped streaming, review, expiry and checklist
outOfScope: Production deployment and case-specific configurable templates

acceptance.description: Bounded, validated private uploads with fail-closed antivirus behavior
acceptance.evidence: Seven focused tests cover size, signatures, body caps, chunks, clean/detected/error scanner responses, and workflow failures with a synthetic socket. The existing private Appwrite bucket accepted a disposable 20 MB file, returned byte-identical content and denied anonymous download. The file was removed.

acceptance.description: Current lead authorization and safe attachment streaming
acceptance.evidence: Synthetic service tests passed assignment, content-role and legacy denial, authorization recheck during handoff, audit-before-stream and attachment headers/bytes. The built dashboard downloaded an attachment through the authorized route.

acceptance.description: Review, expiry, checklist and orphan reconciliation
acceptance.evidence: Synthetic tests passed stale and cross-lead review denial, Pakistan expiry boundaries, pagination, rollback after definite rejection, and preservation on ambiguous acknowledgment. Browser confirmed pending/ready/expired checklist states and review notes. Operator recovery steps are documented.

Built-app browser workflow passed synthetic upload, review, expiry, scanner rejection and attachment download. Typecheck, 111 tests and build passed. Additive Appwrite setup was previewed and actual daemon/proxy verification is documented as a release gate.

nextActions.action: Archive DOC-01 and start TEAM-01 team roles and deactivation. Verify owner protections, lead transfer, session revocation and profile persistence failures.
Before document rollout, apply the additive schema, configure the trusted ClamAV socket and run the real daemon and proxy smoke checks in the release environment.

knownRisks: Appointment/case reminder adapters remain separately gated; external provider delivery is not configured.
Crash-left cycle/lead locks fail closed; recovery requires stopping their owners before targeted operator removal. No expiry takeover.
Task creation/change audit acknowledgments can be ambiguous; inspect recorded task ID/current version before retrying to avoid duplicate work.
Reminder inbox scans 25 stored records per page; task lists still cap at 100. Recurrence/escalation/snooze and provider outbox remain follow-up features.
Runtime health is stale after three minutes without a recorded cycle; a long cycle or delayed clock can also cause stale status. No external alerting provider is configured.
VPS deployment, Nginx/TLS/PM2 reboot smoke checks and production worker activation remain unperformed.
Development branch still contains unaccepted team/reporting modules; whole-branch main merge is gated.

Application ownership transfer is multi-record and not transactional; an interrupted handoff can leave metadata ahead of the lead owner. Existing current-lead scope checks hide records from the wrong counselor; retry/reconciliation still needs feature acceptance.
Scheduling writes share one calendar lock. Partial handoffs may need operator retry, and moved slots remain reserved on the target calendar while the lead remains with its prior owner.
DOC-01 requires three additive Appwrite attributes and a trusted configured ClamAV daemon. Actual daemon acceptance and target-host smoke checks are pending.
Legacy files have no scan marker and require a scanned replacement before download or review. Uncertain uploads require the targeted operator procedure.
